reason: This passage from Exodus 3 portrays the Hebrews (Israelites) as an enslaved people in Egypt, not as a nation with its own specific land. The text describes God commissioning Moses to lead 'my people, the children of Israel' out of Egyptian bondage (מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם). The narrative focuses on liberation from Egypt and service to God at Mount Horeb, but contains no depiction of the Hebrews possessing or inhabiting a specific land of their own. They are presented as oppressed foreigners requiring rescue, not as a landed nation.
